elena: Heads-up — after yesterday's mixed-precision kernel rollout I'm seeing sporadic NaNs during long-chat workloads. Reproducer attached in thread below. :eyes:
sam: Ugh. Seen anything in logs? stack traces?
elena: Quick log excerpt:
```
WARNING: kernel_gemm4b_quant: overflow detected, scale inf
RuntimeError: nan in softmax at torch/csrc...
```
jia: Any pattern on seq len / batch size?
elena: Only on >2048 tokens and when KV cache hits full reuse path (heavy prefix reuse). Small batches ok.
ryan: Could be the FP8/INT8 fused KV kernels selecting quant path at compile-time for those shapes. Kernel selector picks int4 gemm when batch*seq % 128 == 0 on A100.
marta: Profiling? `perf` or our internal flame graphs?
elena: Ran a quick profile with perf-bot: `perf-bot: profile 1750001234 --model redwood-7b-mq --quant int8 --seq 3072 --batch 4` -> attached flame. Hotspot is `kv_attention_kernel_int8_fused` and `pack_weights_int8` with many fastpaths.
sam: Two hypotheses: 1) calibration scale drift over long sequences (accumulated exponent overflow), 2) batch packing edge-case triggers unfinished zeroing of accumulator buffers.
jia: Also saw similar in dev when using per-tensor vs per-channel scales — per-tensor gave more NaNs but slightly faster. Per-channel more stable.
ryan: Temporary mitigation: prefer fp16 KV kernels for seq>1024 or when prefix_reuse_ratio > 0.6. We can change kernel selector to bias against int4/8 for KV ops. Trade: ~1.2-1.4x token cost.
marta: Can we add runtime NaN detector that does a single-check on the first token after a batch switch and fall back to FP16 if detected? Minimal overhead.
elena: I implemented a quick patch locally: if any(isnan) or isinf on KV cache page -> evict and re-run with FP16 kernel. Works in repro. Perf hit ~30% for affected sessions but prevents crash.
sam: Long-term fixes: 1) add smoothquant-style calibration during compile: per-channel linear rescaling with small bias to keep activations in representable range; 2) clamp accumulators with configurable clip threshold; 3) improve packing to zero leftover lanes.
jia: For smoothquant, need a light calibration pass over typical prompts (50-100 steps) — will add to model onboarding pipeline. Impact on perf should be minimal at runtime.
ryan: Also add invariant checks in kernel selection: if kernel historically produced NaNs in production for a model, mark it as 'unstable' for that model/shape combo and exclude until manual review.
marta: Can we automate A/B canary: route 5% of traffic through mixed-precision with tight health checks (nan/inf counters) and kill rollout if >0.1% failures?
elena: Yes. I'll open an infra PR to add canary policy and the runtime NaN fallback.
sam: For triage: please upload a compact repro (one script + seed) to the incident thread, include perf profile and memory dumps. Also add unit tests that force kernel fallback path.
elena: Working on that now. Repro command I'm using: `python tools/repro.py --model redwood-7b-mq --quant int8 --seq 3072 --batch 4 --prompt-file tests/long_prefix.txt`
perf-bot: scheduled perf run 1750001234 -> queued on ci/perf.
ryan: TL;DR: disable int4/8 KV kernel for long-seq by default, add smoothquant calibration in onboarding, runtime NaN detector + FP16 fallback, and canary rollout. Anyone opposed? :thumbsup:
sam: +1
jia: +1
marta: +1
elena: +1 :relieved:
